reason: POV reproduced before patching, no longer reproduced after patching, regressions passed, verifier accepted.

project.cwe_name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

ground_truth.cwe_name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

parsed_output.evidence: Root cause / sink: AbstractUnArchiver.extractFile(File srcF, File dir, InputStream, String entryName, ...) in src/main/java/org/codehaus/plexus/archiver/AbstractUnArchiver.java. Line 309: `final File f = FileUtils.resolveFile( dir, entryName );` resolves an archive-controlled entryName against the extraction directory with no path-traversal / containment check. Trust boundary: entryName originates from an untrusted archive (tar or zip) supplied as AbstractUnArchiver's sourceFile — attacker-controlled archive content crosses into filesystem write operations. Three concrete sink operations off the same unchecked f/dirF all must be guarded: (1) line 313 overwrite/lastModified check on the unvalidated path; (2) lines 319-322 `final File dirF = f.getParentFile(); if (dirF != null) { dirF.mkdirs(); }` creating arbitrary parent directories outside the destination tree; (3) line ~338 `out = new FileOutputStream( f );` writing attacker-controlled content to the unvalidated resolved path (arbitrary file write / potential RCE via overwriting scripts, cron files, etc.). All three sinks are reached from TWO distinct untrusted sources that funnel entryName into this same sink: TAR (TarUnArchiver.java:113 te.getName() -> AbstractUnArchiver.java:304/309/319/322/338, exercised directly by this PoV) and ZIP (AbstractZipUnArchiver.java lines 93-95 ZipEntryFileInfo.getName() using UnicodePathExtraField or zipEntry.getName() -> line 178 -> lines 218/222 extractFileIfIncluded -> the identical AbstractUnArchiver sink, NOT exercised by this PoV but sharing the identical root cause/vulnerable method). Verified empirically: running the PoV against baseline code writes the marker file to workRoot/pov-escaped-marker.txt (outside dest/) and exits 0. Inserting a containment check immediately after FileUtils.resolveFile(dir, entryName) (rejecting any resolved path not equal to or under dir) causes the PoV to throw ArchiverException and exit 1; this experimental patch was reverted afterward (confirmed via git diff/grep — no product/test files remain modified).
parsed_output.expected_vulnerable_behavior: On unpatched code, extracting a TAR archive containing an entry named "../pov-escaped-marker.txt" through the real org.codehaus.plexus.archiver.tar.TarUnArchiver public API writes the file OUTSIDE the destination directory (into the parent of dest/), because AbstractUnArchiver.extractFile() resolves entryName via FileUtils.resolveFile(dir, entryName) with no containment check before creating parent directories (dirF.mkdirs()) and opening the output stream (new FileOutputStream(f)). The PoV asserts the escaped marker file exists outside dest and exits 0 in that case (vulnerable), or 1 if extraction was rejected/contained (patched).
parsed_output.notes: The PoV targets the tar trace (alert groups 1 and 3: TarUnArchiver.java:113 -> AbstractUnArchiver.java:304/309/313 and .../319/322/338) because it is the shortest, most direct source-to-sink path in the alert and requires no plexus-container DI (TarUnArchiver is instantiated directly and driven through its public extract() API with only a ConsoleLogger). Alert group 2's zip traces (AbstractZipUnArchiver.java lines 93-95/178/218/222 -> AbstractUnArchiver.java:304/309/319/322) converge on the exact same AbstractUnArchiver.extractFile() sink and are not separately exercised by this PoV, but are documented in evidence/regression_hint since a fix scoped only to the tar call site would leave the zip path exploitable. Verified live in the project container via the docker wrapper: exit 0 on baseline (vulnerable), exit 1 after an experimental containment-check patch, which was then reverted, leaving the working tree clean except for the new .security-pipeline/pov/ files (PovPathTraversal.java, run_pov.sh).
parsed_output.regression_hint: Invariant a correct fix must enforce: for every archive entry (tar and zip alike), the File returned by resolving entryName against the destination directory (currently FileUtils.resolveFile(dir, entryName) at AbstractUnArchiver.java:309) must have a canonical/normalized path equal to dir or strictly nested beneath it (canonicalPath.startsWith(dir.getCanonicalPath() + File.separator)), checked BEFORE any of: the overwrite/lastModified check (~line 313), dirF.mkdirs() (~line 322), SymlinkUtils.createSymbolicLink/f.mkdirs() for directory entries, and new FileOutputStream(f) (~line 338). On violation, extraction of that entry must fail (throw ArchiverException) or be skipped — not silently written outside destDirectory. Because both TarUnArchiver and AbstractZipUnArchiver funnel into this single extractFile() method, the fix should live in (or be invoked from) AbstractUnArchiver.extractFile() itself so it covers both call sites; a fix applied only at one call site (e.g. only in TarUnArchiver) would leave the zip path exploitable and vice versa. Known bypass variants the fix must also block: plain "../" traversal (used here), nested "../../../", absolute path entry names (e.g. "/etc/cron.d/evil"), Windows-style backslash traversal ("..\\..\\evil"), entries using the Unicode Extra Field path (AbstractZipUnArchiver.java line 94, new String(unicodePath.getUnicodeName(), "UTF-8")) which can encode a different traversing name than zipEntry.getName(), and symlink entries (symlinkDestination) that could point outside destDirectory even when the entry name itself is contained (SymlinkUtils.createSymbolicLink(f, new File(symlinkDestination)) — a related sink not covered by this PoV that a comprehensive fix should also validate).
parsed_output.summary: Created a working PoV proving CWE-022 path traversal ("tar slip"/"zip slip") in plexus-archiver's AbstractUnArchiver.extractFile(), reached via TarUnArchiver. A crafted tar entry named "../pov-escaped-marker.txt" is extracted through the real public TarUnArchiver.extract() API and lands outside the destination directory. Verified: PoV exits 0 on unpatched baseline code and exits 1 when a containment check is inserted at the resolveFile() call site (experimental patch applied, verified, then fully reverted — working tree is clean except for the new .security-pipeline/pov/ files).

parsed_output.patch_notes: Added a private helper `assertWithinDestination(File destination, File target, String entryName)` to AbstractUnArchiver that canonicalizes both paths and throws ArchiverException unless target.equals(destination) or target is nested under destination (startsWith(destPath + File.separator)). Called it right after `final File f = FileUtils.resolveFile(dir, entryName);` in extractFile(), before the overwrite check, dirF.mkdirs(), symlink creation, directory creation, and FileOutputStream write — i.e. before every sink reachable from that resolved path. No other call sites needed changes since both TarUnArchiver.execute() and AbstractZipUnArchiver's extractFileIfIncluded() already call this shared extractFile() method. Added PathTraversalExtractionTest.java with two tests (tar and zip) building a malicious archive with entry name "../escaped-*-marker.txt" and asserting extraction throws ArchiverException and no file lands outside the destination directory.
parsed_output.risk_notes: Low risk: the added check only rejects entries whose resolved canonical path falls outside the destination directory — a case that was never a legitimate use (valid archives always extract within dest). Confirmed no behavioral regression via the full existing test suite (151/151 pass), including SymlinkTest, which specifically exercises symlink entries whose *link target* points outside the destination — that behavior is preserved because the fix only validates the entry's own resolved file location (f), not the symlink target, since constraining the symlink target broke that pre-existing, intentionally-supported test. A more aggressive fix could also validate symlink targets and directory-entry mkdirs targets identically to file entries, but that would require a product decision about whether cross-directory symlinks are supported functionality (current tests say yes) versus a hardening opportunity — flagging this as a possible follow-up but out of scope for a minimal fix that preserves existing behavior.
parsed_output.summary: Fixed CWE-022 path traversal ("tar slip"/"zip slip") in plexus-archiver's shared extraction sink, AbstractUnArchiver.extractFile(). The method resolved archive-controlled entryName via FileUtils.resolveFile(dir, entryName) with no containment check before the overwrite check, parent-directory creation (mkdirs), and FileOutputStream write. Added a canonical-path containment check (assertWithinDestination) immediately after the resolve, before any of those three sinks, throwing ArchiverException when the resolved target is not equal to or nested under the destination directory. Both TarUnArchiver and AbstractZipUnArchiver (including its Unicode-extra-field entry name path) funnel through this exact method, so the single fix covers every trace in the alert plus same-class bypass variants (../, nested ../../, absolute paths, backslash traversal) since canonicalization normalizes them all. Verified the provided POV now exits 1 (contained) instead of 0 (escaped). I also tried adding a containment check on symlink link targets (mentioned as a related sink in the finder evidence), but reverted it after confirming it broke the project's own SymlinkTest, which intentionally creates/extracts symlinks pointing outside the destination directory as existing supported behavior — that sink is outside the alert's actual traces, so the fix stays scoped to the entryName resolution sink shared by all reported traces. Added a regression test (PathTraversalExtractionTest) exercising both a malicious tar entry and a malicious zip entry named "../escaped-marker.txt" through the real TarUnArchiver/ZipUnArchiver public APIs, asserting ArchiverException is thrown and no file is written outside the destination directory. Full mvn test suite: 151/151 passing (149 pre-existing + 2 new), BUILD SUCCESS.

parsed_output.diff_review: Diff is minimal and scoped: one product file changed (AbstractUnArchiver.java, +35/-0) plus one new test file. No modification to the PoV files (.security-pipeline/pov/* only added, untouched/unmodified — pov.diff shows only new files, no edits to existing product code from the PoV stage). The fix is placed at the single shared sink (extractFile) that both TarUnArchiver and AbstractZipUnArchiver call, so it addresses every trace listed in the alert (tar getName() path and zip getName()/UnicodePathExtraField path) without needing per-callsite duplication. The check uses canonical paths and a strict startsWith(destPath + File.separator) test, which correctly handles ../ traversal, nested ../../, absolute paths, and backslash-based traversal after canonicalization. The patcher explicitly considered and declined to extend the check to symlink targets, documenting that doing so broke the pre-existing SymlinkTest which intentionally supports symlinks pointing outside destDirectory — that sink is not part of the reported alert traces, so leaving it out is a reasonable, justified scoping decision rather than an omission. No unrelated behavior changes, no broad refactors, no disabling of functionality.
parsed_output.pov_result: Reran `bash .security-pipeline/pov/run_pov.sh` independently via the docker wrapper against the patched worktree: extraction now throws ArchiverException ("Entry '../pov-escaped-marker.txt' is outside the execution destination directory..."), the escaped marker file does not exist outside dest, and the script prints "[POV] SAFE" and exits 1 — matching the orchestrator's reported pov_after_patch result and confirming the original POV no longer reproduces the vulnerability.
parsed_output.regression_result: Reran `mvn -B test` independently via the docker wrapper: 151 tests run, 0 failures, 0 errors, 1 skipped (pre-existing skip, unrelated), BUILD SUCCESS — matching the orchestrator's reported regression_1 result. This includes SymlinkTest (6/6 pass, confirming legitimate symlink-crossing-directory behavior is preserved) and the new PathTraversalExtractionTest (2/2 pass).
parsed_output.summary: The patch adds a containment check (assertWithinDestination) in AbstractUnArchiver.extractFile() immediately after FileUtils.resolveFile(dir, entryName), before any filesystem side effect (overwrite check, mkdirs, symlink/dir creation, FileOutputStream write). It canonicalizes both the destination and resolved entry path and throws ArchiverException if the entry resolves outside the destination. Since both TarUnArchiver and AbstractZipUnArchiver funnel through this single shared method, the fix covers all reported alert traces (tar and zip) with one minimal change. A regression test (PathTraversalExtractionTest) was added exercising both tar and zip malicious entries through the real public APIs.
